blocks.text: 3. For most Greeks שפן saphan is χοιρογρύλλιος [choirogryllios]. This rendering is the most widely accepted, and accordingly also the most ancient. For so the Elders render it in Levit. XI, 5., Deut. XIV, 7. and Prov. XXX, 26. Moreover, in Psalm. CIII, (Hebraeis CIV,) 18., in place of τοῖς λαγωοῖς [tois lagōois], all the others, that is, Aquila, Symmachus, Theodotion, etc., translated with the similar word χοιρογρυλλίους [choirogryllious], as Jerome testifies in his Epistle to Sunia. From there it also crept into some copies of the Elders. And following the same, the Ethiopic translator of the Pentateuch, in a manuscript at Rome, has for השפן ኮርገሊሎን፡ choerogryllion. But this, I would almost say, is to explain the unknown by the more unknown. For it is not sufficiently established what the χοιρογρύλλιος [choirogryllios] is, since those of the ancients who wrote about animals, Aristotle, for instance, Pliny, Aelian, Oppian, Philes, etc., say nothing whatever about it. Yet the Scholiast on Aristophanes, on the Peace, acknowledges that the word is Greek; but about it he has only this: Ἔστι δὲ ζῶον, ὃ καλεῖται ὑπό τινων χοιρογρύλλιος [Esti de zōon, ho kaleitai hypo tinōn choirogryllios]; It is an animal which is called choerogryllius by some. Other ancient Lexicographers interpret it as the hedgehog or the porcupine. Hesychius: Χοιρογρύλλιον· ὁ ἐχῖνος [Choirogryllion; ho echinos]. The Glosses of Philoxenus: Χοιρογρύλλιος, ἤγουν ἐχῖνος χερσαῖος [Choirogryllios, ēgoun echinos chersaios], Erinacius [hedgehog]. Suidas: Χοιρογρύλλιος· ὕστριξ, ἀκανθόχοιρος, τουτέστιν ἐχῖνος χερσαῖος [Choirogryllios; hystrix, akanthochoiros, toutestin echinos chersaios]. Moreover, the Vulgate translator at Psal. CIII, (Hebraeis CIV,) 18. has The rock is a refuge for the hedgehogs, that is, τοῖς χοιρογρυλλίοις [tois choirogrylliois]; and so too Jerome in his version of the Psalms, which is extant among his Works and in many places differs entirely from the Vulgate. And Eucherius, in the book On the Hebrew Names, chapter 12: Hedgehogs are called chirogrylli, etc. And Vincent, in the Doctrinale, book 16, chapter 86: The hedgehog, which is also called cirogryllus, is an animal having the form of a piglet, but spiny, etc. And the Greek Scholiast on Proverbs, most absurdly: οἱ χοιρογρύλλιοι· εἶδος ἰχθύος, ἤτοι οἱ λαγωοὶ, ἢ οἱ καλούμενοι οἶστροι [hoi choirogryllioi; eidos ichthyos, ētoi hoi lagōoi, ē hoi kaloumenoi oistroi]. Choerogryllii: a species of fish, or hares, or what are called gadflies.
